title: Contract Pricing Agreement Final Rebate Check: Returned Payment Holdback
content:
Returned payment holdback on a Contract Pricing Agreement final rebate check

The returned-payment holdback follows the customer payments the bank returned on the customer's Commercial Credit Account less than 12 whole months before the handling date, each counted by its ledger date. Whole months between two dates are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is earlier than the earlier date's.

- 2 or more returned payments hold back 3 percent of the unpaid rebate balance.
- Exactly one returned payment (at least one and fewer than 2) holds back 1 percent of it.
- No returned payment holds back no returned-payment holdback.

The amount is held back from the unpaid rebate balance before the final check's floor at 0.00, its rounding to the cent and its minimum payout test are applied; what is held back stays in the rebate balance.

Hypothetical example: one returned payment in the window against an unpaid balance of 4000.00 holds back 40.00; two hold back 120.00.
